item: Row 434: the writer reads an article's stored keywords as columns, not ORM objects
summary: index_article's keyword prefetch was 46.4% of writer time at 150k articles (lane F py-spy), mostly ORM row building. It now reads (id, normalized_term, language, is_entity) with a Core select, keeps the lowest-id and language rules, and upgrades a ref to an entity with an ORM-enabled UPDATE. Results are identical (differential tests against the old read; golden output digest equal in the lock env; indexer pin --same, no version bump, so an update re-extracts nothing). Measured on 2 CPUs, 300k-term Zipf vocabulary, 100 terms per article: prefetch 2.00 to 1.27 ms per article at 45-50k articles (-37%), whole index_article 10.14 to 9.11 ms (-10%); with inline counters at 30-35k: prefetch 2.00 to 1.32 ms, index_article 16.90 to 16.04 ms (-5%).
